en: Hmph. I'm sure you heard a mouthful. Or earful. Whatever.
You see, our paper's doing a feature on baseball's waning popularity. I figured I'd backtrack a bit and see where it started⑬and of course, I can't do that without you.
Your sign stealing is what brought match fixing under public scrutiny. That debacle drove a lot of fans from the game itself.
Wow, you really think that makes me want to talk to you? Huh, Kurosaki sure knows how to pick 'em.
Let me put it as plainly as I can. You're not getting an interview, and I don't want to see your face ever again.
Oh, come on. The statute of limitations has run out, hasn't it? Just admit you stole signs and get over it already.
Now tell me. How much did you get for betraying the sport? Didn't you feel any remorse?
The manager was in on it, wasn't he? That's the sort of juicy news our readers love. We'll pay good money for every tidbit you tell us. Okay?
Oh, so you're ignoring me now? Still hanging onto your tattered sense of pride?
All right, then. Why don't we settle this on the diamond!
Come on. I was once a pitcher, and a Wyvern. If you can get past me, I'll give up on that interview. And rest assured, you'll never see me again.
That's a negative. Win or lose, I have nothing to say to the press.
Fine by me. You're not willing to give me the time of day anyhow.
Besides, we're both former pros. I think I can learn a lot more from pitching against you than hearing you talk.
You think you're that special, huh? Okay, say I do win. Will you really get gone for good?
Yeppity-doo. I don't need to say it twice, do I?
Here's the deal. I'm gonna throw ten pitches. Make five of those home runs, and I'll be out of your life faster than you can sing "Take Me Out to the Ballgame."
Only ten pitches? You must be out of practice if that's all you can throw at me.
Hey, I've been retired for years. But for these ten throws, I'll be as good as I was back in my heyday. You can count on that.
Hah, who woulda thunk it? Two former Wyverns, duking it out at a dinky little batting cage... both of us having descended into lowly newsmongers, no less.
At least people care about <Italic>my</Italic> news. Now will you quit pestering me?
Yeah, I suppose that was the deal. Fine. Consider me a stranger. Oh, but first... I guess I owe you an interview fee.
What's this for? I gave you no such interview.
You're right. You gave me something better. I can clearly see your batting hasn't rotted away. You still have what it takes to be in the pros.
Even after all these years, you still kept practicing your swing, in spite of your permanent ban. That's some dedication.
You practice in hopes of making a comeback some day. You wouldn't bother to do that unless you were truly innocent.
And because you know that in your heart, you have the resolve to press on. You're convinced your innocence will be proven one day. Correct me if I'm wrong.
What'd you say your name was? Asada? I'd say you have more talent with a pen than a ball. That's quite the compelling narrative.
I guess I'll take that as a compliment, but it doesn't make me happy one bit.
No, I'm sure it doesn't. Hence why I said it.
Haha. You're a cruel man, Shinada.
Hey, Asada-san! Don't tell me you're taking his side now!?
What the hell is going on!? Why can't anyone keep a grudge against this jackass?
Kurosaki... Why are you still holding on to yours?
Sorry to disappoint, but I write for a small gossip paper. Our readers are hardly sophisticated enough to understand the tear-jerking redemption of a fallen hero.
Still, you did provide me with a lead. I'd be happy to spot you for a coffee break at least.
Now if you'll excuse me, Kurosaki-san. I hope you'll give my readers something they can actually chew on next time.
Little shithead.
Welp, I'm out of here, too. I'm sick of you creeping up on me.
Oh, and Kurosaki. Wise up, man. You can't be pulling people's strings forever. It's gonna snap right back at you.
Mind your own goddamn business! If you only knew...
And Asada takes the win! I'll be back for that interview, Shinada-san.
Hey there, Shinada-san, it is <Italic>me</Italic>. Thought you'd be in the mood for an interview this time around.
Didn't I tell you no already?
I'm not the type to take that for an answer. If you can beat me on the diamond, I'll stop coming around.
I would love that. All right, I'll take you on.
You said that already!
Then let's have at it!
Hey. Shinada.
Oh, just Kurosaki again. What a surprise. What are you scheming this time?
Quit yapping and come with me.
Yeah, no thanks. Why would I do that? I got enough problems already.
Heh, so you're a coward, then? Don't worry, I won't lay a finger on you, I swear.
Yeah? Then what are you planning?
Come with me and see for yourself.
(All right. Might as well see what he wants, at least for old times' sake.)
You gonna try again, or am I gonna have to drag your ass out there?
Oh I'll be there, Kurosaki. And it won't be a repeat of last time.
There he is. Took you long enough.
You just keep popping out of nowhere, don't you?
I sure do. Now today we settle the score. Follow me.
Can you really replicate Akamatsu's pitching, though? Have you consulted with your shoulder first?
Stop with the shoulder talk and come with me, all right? We'll talk when we're there.
I've been waiting a long time for this, Shinada.
Then I won't keep you any longer. This time's gonna be different.
That's fine. Please come again soon.
Hello. May I take your order?
(Okay, it's fishing time!)
If you don't get a bite, you lose the bait you used and have to start over. Select bait suited to the depth where the fish seem to be.
Once you cast your line, wait for a fish to bite. Watch the float carefully. As soon as it bobs down, press <Action:Button_Cross@Fishing_River> to quickly pull your pole up.
Some fish will fight hard. Press <Action:Button_Cross@Fishing_River> rapidly if you find it difficult to raise your pole.
(Better check the instructions.)

The buttons in the four sections of the cursor <Action:Button_Circle@Cost_Of_A_Swing><Action:Button_Triangle@Cost_Of_A_Swing><Action:Button_Square@Cost_Of_A_Swing><Action:Button_Cross@Cost_Of_A_Swing> are the swing buttons. Move the cursor to the ball and swing by pressing one of those buttons.

This cursor is called the swing cursor. Move it using <Action:Button_LS_Left@Cost_Of_A_Swing><Action:Button_LS_Right@Cost_Of_A_Swing><Action:Button_LS_Up@Cost_Of_A_Swing><Action:Button_LS_Down@Cost_Of_A_Swing>.
The smaller areas inside the swing cursor are the slugging ranges.
You will hit the ball much more powerfully if you hit it within a slugging range.
The ball's anticipated location is indicated by the pink area.
While this is only a guess, it will still provide a general idea of where the ball will be.
Make perfect contact by swinging right when the ball and anticipated course turn yellow.

Move the cursor to this area, then press the corresponding button <Action:Button_Circle@Cost_Of_A_Swing><Action:Button_Triangle@Cost_Of_A_Swing><Action:Button_Square@Cost_Of_A_Swing><Action:Button_Cross@Cost_Of_A_Swing> at the right time to hit the ball.

(So what should I eat?)
(What should I have?)
Thanks for comin'. Stop by again soon!
Hmm. Usually I'd get the uni, but today I think I'll get the <Color:8>Special Sushi Zanmai<Color:Default>.
(Guess Kaguya wants the <Color:8>Special Sushi Zanmai<Color:Default>.)
The fish here is so fresh and delicious! There's nothing better than eating sushi made to order!
Don't ya get out much? Sounds like you haven't been out to eat in a while.
That's true. I usually cook for myself at home, or else I'll order delivery.
You get stuff like sushi and soba delivered?
Sushi is expensive, so I hardly order it. And I've never ordered soba before.
Well, then whaddya get delivered?
Stuff like curry or pizza.
They have that? Guess they got everythin' nowadays.
It's not particularly recent. They've had these things for quite some time, you know.
There are fast food places that deliver burgers, and even convenience stores offer delivery now.
Really? I guess with that kinda convenience I can see why people wind up as shut-ins.
Yep. That's why when I do go out to eat, I don't make the food my main focus. What's more important is spending time with whoever I'm with.
I see. So it's not the meal that's important, it's where ya go to get it?
Yes. That's why no matter how good delivery options get, I don't think eating out is ever going away for me.
Yeah, I can see what ya mean. You're pretty smart.
When I'm killing time at home, this is the sort of thing I always think about.
I'm not a fan of delivery. Even if they offer a whole buncha different things, I figure I'm better off at a restaurant.
Oh? Why is that?
Delivery takes too long, especially when I'm hungry. I need to eat right away.
Then why not try to put an order in ahead of time?
That ain't all it is. For example, with sushi, I can pick my own fish with my own eyes, or ask the sushi chef for recommendations.
Ya can't do any of that with delivery. And ya can't add more to your order later either.
Ah! I can see how you wouldn't be able to do that with delivery.
Plus you can get to know the restaurant staff too, so it's way better.
Yer gonna get fat. If you're not gonna leave home, ya may as well eat somethin' healthy.
So to ask you the same question, is it okay to eat fatty foods when eating out?
Nah, that ain't what I mean. The time it takes to walk someplace is exercise, right? It's a bit healthier than delivery.
That's not a very convincing argument. If I'm looking after my health, I should still make a point to eat only healthy foods when eating out.
Someone who can't be consistent about eating healthy isn't persuasive at all.
You might not agree with me, but do ya at least see the reasonin' behind what I'm sayin'?
Reasoning? Then why don't I just exercise indoors at home?
Ya've got a comeback for everythin', don't you?
Uncle Kaz, I'd really like the <Color:8>Uni<Color:Default>.
(Haruka wants to have the <Color:8>Uni<Color:Default>.)
But I wanted the <Color:8>Uni<Color:Default>...
Thanks, Uncle Kaz! This looks really tasty!
